problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a=⟨0,5⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(3,-3)$ and has velocity $⟨1,0⟩$ when $t=2,$ calculate the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$

examples.problem:
The acceleration $\mathbf{a}$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
\mathbf{a}(t) =  \left<   9\cos {3t},\, \sin{t} \right>.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(0,0)$ and has velocity $\left\langle 2,\,0  \right\rangle$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$
examples.worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector. To find the velocity vector, we first need to integrate the acceleration vector. 

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,\text{d}t,\,\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t+{C}_{1},\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $\mathbf{v} (0)= \langle 2,\, 0 \rangle.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0) & =⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡0+{C}_{1},\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡0+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨2,\,0⟩ & =⟨{C}_{1},-1+{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have $C_1=2$ and $C_2=1.$ Therefore, the velocity vector is

$$
\mathbf{v}(t) = \left<      3\sin{3t} +2 , \,    1-\cos{t} \right>.
$$

We can compute the position vector by integrating the velocity vector.

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t+2,\,1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t+2\,\text{d}t,\,\int 1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡3t+2t+{C}_{3},\,t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{C}_{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $\mathbf{r} (0)= \langle 0,0 \rangle.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡0+2(0)+{C}_{3},\,0-\operatorname{sin}⁡0+{C}_{4}⟩ \\ ⟨0,0⟩ & =⟨-1+{C}_{3},\,{C}_{4}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have $C_3=1$ and $C_4=0.$ Therefore, the position of $P$ at time $t$ is

$$
\mathbf{r}(t) = \left<  -\cos {3t} + 2t + 1 , \,   t-\sin{t}  \right>.
$$

feedback.problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v(t)=⟨4t,3{t}^{2}-1⟩\,,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Given that the particle is at the position  $r=⟨-2,0⟩$ when $t=0,$ calculate the times when the particle is at the origin.
feedback.worked_solution:
The particle is at the origin when its position is $r=⟨0,0⟩.$ So first, we need to compute the position function of the particle.

To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨4t,3{t}^{2}-1⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 4t\,\text{d}t,\,\int (3{t}^{2}-1)\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨2{t}^{2}+{C}_{1},\,{t}^{3}-t+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(0)=⟨-2,0⟩.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨2(0)^{2}+{C}_{1},\,{0}^{3}-0+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨-2,0⟩ & =⟨{C}_{1},\,{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=-2$ and ${C}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the position of $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨2{t}^{2}-2,\,{t}^{3}-t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the times at which the particle is at the origin, we solve the equation $r(t)=⟨0,0⟩.$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨0,0⟩ \\ ⟨2{t}^{2}-2,\,{t}^{3}-t⟩ & =⟨0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So we need

$$
\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}-2=2(t-1)(t+1) & =0\,⇒\,t=\pm 1, \\ {t}^{3}-t=t(t-1)(t+1) & =0\,⇒\,t=\pm 1,0.\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions that satisfy both equations are $t=\pm 1.$ Therefore, we conclude that the particle is at the origin  when $t=\pm 1.$
